title: Solutions: Chapter Introduction
subject: Chemistry
objective: Soda fizzes when opened and the sea does not freeze at 0 °C: both are solution behaviour. The chapter covers concentration, Henry's and Raoult's laws and colligative properties.

num.q: Find the molarity of a solution with 0.5 mol of NaCl in 2 L of solution.
Find the molality of 4 g of NaOH (molar mass 40 g mol⁻¹) in 500 g of water.
18 g of glucose (180 g mol⁻¹) is dissolved in 90 g of water (18 g mol⁻¹). Find the mole fraction of glucose.

short.q: State Henry's law and use it to explain why soda fizzes on opening.
short.solution: The partial pressure of a gas above a solution is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution (p = K_H x). Soda is bottled under high CO₂ pressure; opening lowers the pressure, so less CO₂ stays dissolved and the excess escapes as bubbles.

short.q: Why does sea water not freeze at 0 °C?
short.solution: Dissolved salts depress the freezing point (a colligative property): the more solute particles, the lower it goes. Sea water freezes at about −1.9 °C.
